question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus / washout with chromatin accessibility tracking
ideas.description: Expose cells to a defined AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA, injury, or inflammatory cue), then wash out and perform time-resolved ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN, and RNA-seq over days to weeks. Persistence of AP-1-dependent open chromatin and primed gene expression after AP-1 activity returns to baseline would indicate memory.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation or dominant-negative block at different phases
ideas.description: Use degron-tagged FOS/JUN or a dominant-negative (A-FOS) to remove AP-1 either during the initial stimulus (encoding) or after the stimulus has faded (maintenance). If blocking during encoding abolishes the enhanced secondary response but removing it later doesn't, AP-1 is needed to establish but not sustain memory; the opposite pattern implies active maintenance.

ideas.title: Primed vs naive re-stimulation response assay
ideas.description: Compare transcriptional output (RNA-seq, nascent transcription via PRO-seq) and kinetics after a second stimulus in previously stimulated versus naive cells, with varying rest intervals. Quantifying faster, stronger, or more sustained induction at AP-1 target genes, and correlating it with AP-1 binding and H3K27ac at their enhancers, tests functional memory.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome lineage tracing of memory inheritance
ideas.description: Use scATAC/RNA multiome with lineage barcodes or sister-cell pairing to test whether AP-1-linked accessibility states and primed expression are inherited through cell divisions in clonal lineages. Heritability of states beyond what cell-type or stochastic variation explains, and bimodality of states, would support a memory mechanism.

ideas.title: Locus-specific perturbation of AP-1 motifs and memory-state engineering
ideas.description: Use CRISPR editing of AP-1 motifs, or dCas9-based recruitment or blocking of AP-1/chromatin remodelers (e.g., SWI/SNF) at candidate enhancers, and optogenetic or pulsed AP-1 activation to write memory artificially. Determining whether motif loss erases memory, and whether a synthetic pulse is sufficient to induce a persistent primed state, tests necessity and sufficiency.
